text:
Colorado out-chanced Dallas 2.64 to 1.87 in expected goals and got 63 shot attempts to 49, which gave the Avalanche a 64 percent share of simulated replays. They still lost in a shootout, with Dallas winning 3-2 at Ball Arena.

The turning point came early in the third. Arttu Hyry scored a shorthanded backhand at 1:20, a 33 percent chance and the best look of any goal in the game, to put the Stars up 2-1. Colorado answered at 8:21 when Brock Nelson scored on a 5 percent chance, and the Avalanche then took over the period, 1.27 expected goals to 0.55. Gabriel Landeskog had a 23 percent look stopped by Casey DeSmith, who turned aside 25 of 27 shots and finished 0.64 goals above expected. Colorado went 0 for 4 on the power play, worth 0.42 expected goals, while Dallas was 0 for 2.

The shootout was Dallas's. Jason Robertson scored in the first round, Nazem Kadri tied it for Colorado in the second, and Roope Hintz scored in the fourth round after Nathan MacKinnon was stopped in the third. Nelson then missed to end it. Scott Wedgewood allowed two goals on 22 shots, almost exactly what the chances called for, so the Avalanche had no goaltending edge to lean on. Colorado had also won the night before, 3-2 in regulation.
